name: child with a limp overview
title: A child with a limp or hip pain: first exclude a septic hip with the Kocher criteria, then age separates transient synovitis, Legg-Calve-Perthes disease and slipped capital femoral epiphysis; each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment

root.title: A child with a limp: is it a SEPTIC hip? If not, AGE narrows the rest
lines: every one: blood count, ESR (erythrocyte sedimentation rate) and CRP (C-reactive protein), hip x-ray ± ultrasound

groups.title: Afebrile and well: AGE decides
lines: under 10: transient synovitis · 4-8: Perthes · teenager: slipped epiphysis

head: h
Transient synovitis
non-infectious hip inflammation after a virus
pres: • SUDDEN hip pain 7-10 days after a cold or sore throat
• afebrile or LOW fever, looks well
hip held flexed, abducted, externally rotated
inv: • NORMAL (ESR, CRP may be slightly up)
• done to rule out septic arthritis

head: h
Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease
avascular necrosis of the femoral head
pres: • pain referred to the KNEE, better with rest
inv: flattened, fragmented femoral head · bone scan, MRI

head: h
Slipped capital femoral epiphysis
the head slips posterior and inferior on the neck
pres: • gradual hip, thigh or KNEE pain
• left more often · 1 in 5 both hips
hip rolls into EXTERNAL rotation on flexion (Drehmann sign)
inv: • Klein's line along the neck MISSES the head

panels.title: The rest of the differential, by age
items: under 4: transient synovitis · infection · juvenile idiopathic arthritis · non-accidental injury · pain referred from the limb
4-10: transient synovitis · Perthes · infection · 10-16: slipped epiphysis · avulsion fracture · infection
uncommon at any age: leukemia and bone tumours

panels.title: Any abnormal gait: warning signs
items: asymmetry · progression · leg length difference · pain · deformity · a suspected associated condition
also: missed hip dysplasia, clubfoot, overuse, trauma (see the PEDIATRIC ORTHOPEDICS chart)
